text:
nina: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting streaming disconnects + immediate reconnects that double-count tokens. This started after last night's edge proxy deploy. Pattern: server emits lots of tiny frames (<50B) and client libs hit onclose 1006.

ash: are these WebSocket only or SSE too?

nina: primarily WS for now, but a couple of SSE clients show partial-event fragmentation. Route: /v1/stream/chat (us-central). Model: rwd-13b-slim.

rajesh: can you paste raw bytes from the proxy logs? curious if framing looks like isolated fragments or truncated utf8.

nina: snippet from proxy packet capture: 

```
--> TCP segment: 48 bytes
payload (hex): 1f 8b 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 03 7b 22 74 6b 22 3a 22 31 22 7d
```

(looks like compressed small chunk containing: {"tk":"1"})

omar: compressed + micro-chunking + http2->ws plumbing could be the culprit. Our proxy has a change that toggled aggressive write flushing in the http2 path.

ash: so two knobs: stop aggressive flush or coalesce at the proxy. Stopping aggressive flush might help other workloads too but could increase tail latency.

rajesh: ops ask: do we have a dashboard that surfaces "reconnect loops"? Right now we only have per-connection error rates.

omar: not yet. I'll add two metrics: `stream.reconnect_rate` and `stream.fragmented_frame_ratio`. Also label by `route` and `tenant_id`.

nina: repro steps for devs: run a simple server that writes small chunks rapidly (server pseudo):

```
// pseudo
while (streaming) { socket.write(Buffer.from('{"tk":"'+seq+'"}')); await sleep(5); }
```

If we proxy through edge with aggressive-flush enabled we hit the symptom. Direct to runtime -> OK.

ash: can we try a quick patch to the proxy: coalesce consecutive writes within 30ms into one WS frame, but skip coalescing if the payload looks like a ping/heartbeat (single-char or just "\n").

rajesh: need feature flag and per-route opt-out. Also add traces so we can see coalesced vs raw frames in the console timeline.

omar: I'll prototype and add a toggle `proxy.coalesce_ws_writes` (default off). We'll run a short canary in staging.

ops-bot: deploy: edge-proxy/staging -> started at 2026-03-23T10:05:00Z (canary id c-1024).

nina: quick check: what about billing dedupe? When clients reconnect mid-stream they often re-send the request and we may bill twice. We need server-idempotency or at least console visibility for "possible double-billed streams".

rajesh: agree. Two mitigations: (1) token-granular dedupe is hard; (2) surface a console flag that flags requests with reconnect history within a TTL (e.g., 5m) as "reconnect-risk". We'll annotate trace view and billing export.

ash: tradeoffs: false positives vs protecting customers. I'm leaning to flag-only first, not automated crediting.

omar: implemented coalesce prototype: buffer up to 128 bytes or 30ms. If accumulated bytes form valid utf8/JSON, forward immediately. Else forward when buffer full or timeout. Includes CLI toggle.

nina: test in staging (small customer subset) reduced reconnects from ~12/min -> ~2/min. Some tail token latency increased 8-12ms in p50/p95.

rajesh: good. can you wire the new metrics to a console panel? UX ask: create a small "Stream health" card on the route page: fields: reconnect rate, fragmented_frame_ratio, coalesce_buffer_latency_ms, impacted_tenants.

omar: on it. Also adding a trace annotation when coalescing happens so SRE can inspect exact frames.

ops-bot: scheduled rollout: 10% @ 2026-03-23T12:30Z -> 40% @ 2026-03-23T13:00Z -> 100% @ 2026-03-23T15:00Z (manual holds between steps).

nina: final note: added a short incident playbook snippet for streaming reconnects to the runbook: steps to validate coalesce toggle, how to query `stream.reconnect_rate`, and how to gift credits if needed.

ash: thanks. Once console tile is live ping #incidents and support so CS can proactively reach affected customers.

rajesh: logging reminder: don't store full frames in telemetry; send hashes + lengths to avoid PII leakage.

omar: PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/omar/edge-proxy-coalesce-ws (WIP). Will attach perf graphs.

nina: staging looks stable after 45m. Holding canary for 2h. Will report back.
